question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} 7\cos\left(4 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=4 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=4\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)=0\\ x=\frac{\pi}{4}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=4\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)+\left(0\right)=\pi.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} 7\cos\left(4 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=7\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)\int_{0}^{\pi} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{7}{4}\int_{0}^{\pi} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{7}{4}\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{0}^{\pi}\\ &=\frac{7}{4}\left(\sin\left(\pi\right)-\sin\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{7}{4}\left(\left(0\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=0.\end{aligned}
$$

\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{9}} 5\cos\left(9 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=9,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
